item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
From the day this was posted, I've felt like it was lacking some sinister core.
A dark cloud to fill out the silver-lining, if you will.
Re-reading years later I've found that sour note.

Simply touching SCP-999’s surface causes an immediate euphoria, which intensifies the longer one is exposed to SCP-999, and lasts long after separation from the creature

Even if we assume physical addiction is not a factor, this lovable galoot would be massively psychologically addictive.

And Foundation administration wants to peddle extracts. Which now puts me in mind of early scenes from The Stuff.
Blissed out consumers lining up to get their fix of tickle-juice, maybe some fistfights breaking out over who's next and who "needs" it more.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: 999 for me really adds to the verisimilitude of the Foundation's world. Naturally this is just my take but I always felt that the various anomalies are more interesting as evidence of a fundamentally chaotic, unpredictable universe rather than an actively malicious one. Given the infinite possibilities of such a chaotic universe the existence of the occasional anomaly that is, well, adorable is inevitable. If every article is terrifying horror then that horror loses it's punch; if everything is scary nothing is.
